verdicts.reason: A: The four-line headline fills the square with strong presence. The bottom row is the problem: the body copy is centre-aligned in a cramped left column and its left edge (~97px) doesn't line up with the headline (~125px), while the CTA sits off to the right. That breaks the original's single centred axis and leaves the bottom crowded under a heavy headline. B: A faithful centred stack with clear hierarchy, readable text and nothing colliding. But it is basically the original lifted onto the square, with large empty orange bands above (~225px) and below (~200px), a single-line subline that runs almost edge to edge, and a slightly jagged edge on the CTA pill. B is cleaner and more coherent overall.
